key_insight: Eliminating stalled, non-contributing operators in ADAPT-VQE and combining the method with correlated downfolding can make variational quantum chemistry both faster and more accurate in a fixed active space.
engineering_relevance: This reduces circuit depth and optimization cost for near-term quantum devices, making ADAPT-VQE more practical for chemistry workloads on limited quantum hardware.
method: Detect and remove plateaued operators from the ansatz pool during optimization.
Compare elimination with and without pool restoration to assess convergence behavior.
Integrate ADAPT-VQE with OBDF to replace the bare active-space Hamiltonian by a correlated effective Hamiltonian.
evidence_signal: Benchmarked in OpenFermion on linear H6 chain, H6 lattice, H6 ring, and N2; the abstract reports faster convergence, lower circuit depth and iteration count, and energies closer to FCI than standard ADAPT-VQE.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable plateau detection and the quality of the downfolded Hamiltonian, so implementation choices may affect robustness across different molecules and active spaces.
paper_title: Reducing quantum resources for ADAPT-VQE via plateau-operator elimination and correlated mean-field downfolding
